title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: 44 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH and 4 GUARD_TOWERs for the Anglo-Saxon player: Harold's army fought an open-field defensive action on the Senlac ridge with no fortifications whatsoever; the engine offered palisades or simply massed infantry, so a stone-walled fortress is an avoidable invention

TOWN_CENTER, MONASTERY, BLACKSMITH, STABLE and ARCHERY_RANGE for both sides turn a one-day field battle into a base-vs-base fight; neither army had installations at Senlac (William's only work was the prefab motte at Hastings, several miles off)
16 SKIRMISHERs in the Saxon roster: contemporary accounts (and the Bayeux Tapestry) show the English fielding essentially no missile troops at Hastings — that was the Norman advantage
Anglo-Saxon STABLE building implies mounted forces; Harold's housecarls dismounted to fight and the shield wall was entirely on foot
4174 TREE_OAK tiles render Senlac as dense forest; the ridge itself was open ground with the Andredsweald at the Saxon rear only
